sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Following the November 3 midterm elections, data centre expansion emerged as a significant political issue. Voters in several states expressed strong opposition to new facilities, citing concerns over environmental damage, local community influence, and the potential for increased utility costs. Despite significant spending by pro-AI groups, candidates opposing rapid data centre development won seats in multiple states.

sections.heading: Why it matters

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Former SAS officer George Simm denied that the unit operated under a shoot-to-kill policy during the Troubles. Simm, who led an ambush in 1988 that resulted in the deaths of three IRA members, stated that soldiers only fired when under direct attack. He criticised the government for failing to support veterans regarding legacy legislation. Conversely, relatives of those killed by the SAS argue that the soldiers could have arrested the men instead of killing them, describing the events as pre-planned shoot-to-kill operations.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The debate highlights ongoing tensions surrounding the legacy of the conflict in Northern Ireland. While the government claims its Troubles Bill provides effective safeguards for veterans, groups like Relatives for Justice argue that the legislation prioritises the interests of those who killed over the rights of victims and survivors.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Amazon and Uber have partnered to integrate Uber Eats into the Amazon platform. Prime members in the US can now order restaurant meals directly via the Amazon app or website without needing a separate Uber account. Amazon manages the ordering process, while Uber Eats facilitates the delivery.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: This collaboration marks Amazon's return to restaurant delivery after previously closing its own service. By partnering, Amazon avoids the high costs of building a delivery network from scratch. For Uber, the deal provides access to millions of Prime subscribers, helping the company compete against its larger rival, DoorDash.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: It remains uncertain if this benefit will significantly influence Prime subscriber behaviour. While the deal removes delivery fees for orders over twenty-five dollars, other costs such as service fees, tips, and menu markups remain, potentially limiting the appeal for casual or solo diners.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Sony recorded net profits of 449.60 billion yen for the quarter ending in September, marking a 44 percent increase year-on-year. gist: Thomas Markle Jr is a person of interest in a child abuse image inquiry.
Philippine authorities are investigating allegations involving Thomas Markle Sr's belongings.
Thomas Markle Jr reported the images to authorities after discovering them.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Thomas Markle Jr has been named a person of interest in a Philippine investigation into child sexual abuse imagery. The inquiry concerns material allegedly found in the belongings of his father, Thomas Markle Sr. While Markle Jr alerted the FBI and local police to the images, authorities are now examining whether he is involved in the crime. Markle Sr, who has denied possessing such imagery, is currently in a care home in the US.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The investigation involves thousands of images depicting minors. Philippine officials have described the material as highly deplorable. The case has drawn attention due to the family connection to the Duchess of Sussex, who has stated she is deeply distressed by the allegations.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Philippine authorities expect to determine the extent of Markle Jr's involvement in the coming days.

The inquiry is based in the Philippines.
Authorities are investigating allegations of child sexual abuse imagery found in storage boxes.

timeline.text: Meet *sshole, the vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices

gist: A decade-old vulnerability dubbed *sshole affects some configurations of Alpine Linux and other distributions.
The flaw allows attackers to log into certain passwordless accounts with no password.
Exploitation requires specific conditions involving OpenSSH, musl, PAM, and password hashing configurations.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A vulnerability in the interaction between OpenSSH, musl, and specific configurations allows attackers to log into Linux devices without a password. Alpine maintainers and security firm Checkpoint reported that the flaw works every time with a single connection when specific conditions are met, including passwordless account settings and particular password hashing functions.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The consequences of the vulnerability are high because attackers reaching the SSH port can gain access without knowing any password. However, root accounts are safe under default settings, though accounts with sudo or doas rights can still elevate privileges.

gist: Aircraft engine turbine blades are grown as a single crystal through a specialized casting process.
Only a handful of companies worldwide can produce these single crystal turbine blades.
China is striving to master the technology, while Western manufacturers maintain a major advantage.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Aircraft engines use hundreds of turbine blades grown from a molten metal alloy into a single crystal. Only a few companies and five countries have perfected this complex manufacturing process. GE Aerospace announced it would acquire its turbine blade supplier, and Rolls-Royce said it would invest in its blade casting facility.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: These hardy blades withstand extreme temperatures and mechanical stresses. The single crystal structure is essential for blade performance, allowing engines to run efficiently. Demand is huge and supply chains are volatile, making the technology a critical component for aircraft manufacturing.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Specialists continue improving blade capabilities, including more intricate cooling passages and reduced mass. China aims to master the technology chain. Meanwhile, high demand for aircraft could drive future competition for engine and turbine blade suppliers.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Montevideo, Uruguay, starting a 12-day tour across Latin America. Upon arrival, he greeted crowds, delivered a speech on healthcare access in Plaza Independencia, and prayed at Montevideo Cathedral.

sections.text: The journey represents the Pope's sixth international trip, covering over 20,000 miles despite recent health concerns. sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A woman from East Sussex named Sheila Williams took on a waitress job for the winter to help pay her bills after her oil bill doubled since the start of 2026. Thousands of homes across Sussex rely on oil rather than the gas mains, facing potential bills of more than £970 for a 1,000-litre tank. Nigel Wanstall from Sheffield Park reported having no heating at all because he cannot afford to fill his oil tank, using an open fire and an electric blanket instead.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The soaring cost of heating oil leaves vulnerable households struggling to afford basic warmth, prompting some residents to take extra work or go without heating entirely. A government spokesperson stated that £53m in support has been pledged for vulnerable households on heating oil and the 4% tariff on home heating oil has been removed.

The Department for Education and several universities pledged to review their information.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The BBC found that 12 universities in England only used below-average salaries in student loan repayment examples on their websites. Some sites also featured inaccurate details about repayment thresholds and write-off dates, while the Department for Education's website lacked real-world examples for Plan 5 students.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Treasury Committee chair Dame Meg Hillier said the information was misleading and compared repayments to minor expenses. Graduates may face higher monthly repayments as their salaries increase over time, meaning initial low estimates can give a false impression of future costs.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The Department for Education stated it would review the information it provides and work with universities. Several universities have already updated their websites or are reviewing their content following the BBC's findings.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Tesla chief executive Elon Musk has announced that production of the Cybertruck will wind down around the middle of next year at its Texas factory. The vehicle launched in 2023 but suffered from disappointing sales, quality issues, delays, and recalls, failing to approach its target of 200,000 annual sales.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The decision marks the end of Tesla's attempt to capture the US pickup market. The Cybertruck never went on sale in Europe after failing to meet safety standards. Musk is now prioritising artificial intelligence, robotics, and autonomous driving over traditional vehicle development.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Tesla will use its factory in Austin, Texas to expand Cybercab production and build the Optimus humanoid robot. The company is also ramping up production of its Semi electric lorry and aims to begin Roadster production in 2028.

quotes.text: We dug our own grave with Cybertruck
Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production.

gist: Tube drivers in the RMT union announced 24-hour strikes over working arrangements.
The industrial action is in opposition to Transport for London plans for a four-day week.
Business groups warned the Christmas run-up strikes would cause significant disruption to commuters and shoppers.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: London Underground drivers in the RMT union announced a series of 24-hour strikes starting on 26 November, with further walkouts planned through December, January and February. The action is in dispute over plans for a voluntary four-day working week, which the RMT opposes. Meanwhile, the Aslef union welcomed the proposals, calling the strike a strange choice.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The RMT argued the plans would worsen shift times, increase driving hours and pave the way for job cuts. Transport for London maintained the changes are voluntary, offer a choice of working pattern, and reduce overall hours. Business groups warned the strikes risk damaging the hospitality sector and vital Christmas trading.

fivew: Tube drivers in the RMT union.

In opposition to plans to introduce a four-day working week.

quotes.text: London Underground is attempting to dress up a wholesale attack on drivers' working conditions as a voluntary four-day week.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Amazon launched a feature allowing selected US customers to text the Alexa shopping assistant. Users can send text messages or photographs of items to search for products, manage lists, compare prices, and complete purchases.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The feature taps into a growing trend of interacting with AI agents through text messages ahead of the holiday shopping season. It follows Amazon blocking another tool in September and competes with similar text-based shopping features from other companies.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Following the initial rollout to a small group, Amazon plans to expand the texting capability to millions more customers in the upcoming weeks. Those without an invite can join a waitlist.

timeline.text: Childminder who left more than 20 children alone in her home jailed

gist: A childminder who left over 20 children unattended was jailed for two years.
Suspicious parents discovered the neglect after watching her leave for a school run.
An internal probe revealed she was likely tipped off about previous inspections.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Amanda Mathewson, a childminder in Dunfermline, was jailed for two years after pleading guilty to wilfully neglecting and abandoning children. Suspicious parents watched her leave for a school run and found over 20 unattended children inside her home in August 2024. Children were found unsupervised, distressed, and in hot rooms without food or water.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The case exposed a gross abuse of trust and severe regulatory failings. The Care Inspectorate admitted Mathewson was likely tipped off about inspections by an insider, compromising regulatory scrutiny and leading families to explore civil action.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: A learning review by the Fife child protection committee will examine potential improvements to practice and processes. The Scottish government is working with independent regulators to enhance transparency, while lawyers represent families exploring a civil case.

fivew: A childminder was jailed for two years for leaving more than 20 children alone and unsupervised.
She pleaded guilty to wilfully neglecting, abandoning and exposing children to unnecessary suffering.

quotes.text: It is beggars belief that a failing of this magnitude could go unnoticed.

gist: Cult leader Paul Mackenzie has been sentenced to 200 years in prison in Kenya.
He was convicted of murdering 191 followers, mostly children, through forced starvation.
Mackenzie faces further legal charges, including terrorism and manslaughter, which he denies.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Paul Mackenzie and 28 accomplices were sentenced in Kenya for murdering 191 people, mostly children, in Shakahola forest. Mackenzie ordered followers to starve their children and themselves to meet Jesus. Outlets differ on timeline details; the Guardian notes mass graves were discovered over three years ago, whereas the BBC reports grave discoveries in 2023.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The deaths highlighted a lack of oversight regarding rogue religious organisations in Kenya. The case has prompted calls for stricter regulation of religious groups across the country.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Mackenzie faces additional charges, including terrorism and manslaughter, alongside ongoing investigations into over 200 further deaths.

gist: David Staff has died aged 68 of a heart condition.

His former apprentice will continue the Suffolk workshop.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: David Staff, a cornetto player, period trumpeter and maker of natural trumpets, has died aged 68 of a heart condition. He learned instrument making from Frank Tomes, eventually taking over the business and establishing a workshop near Coddenham in Suffolk. Staff was also a founder member of His Majestys Sagbutts & Cornetts and a long-serving principal trumpet in the Orchestra of the Eighteenth Century.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Staff was a significant figure in the early music revival of the late 20th century. He was widely respected for his high-register playing, refined interpretations, and his craft in making natural trumpets from flat sheets of brass. He also made a major contribution to music education, teaching at the Royal Northern College of Music and the Conservatorium van Amsterdam.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The workshop will be continued by his former apprentice and hand engraver of 11 years.

stories.title: Doctors pull knife from man's eye that went through his brain—and he's fine now
stories.standfirst: It's the exact path, not the apparent severity that matters most, doctors say.

articles.title: Doctors pull knife from man's eye that went through his brain—and he's fine now
articles.standfirst: It's the exact path, not the apparent severity that matters most, doctors say.

timeline.text: Man unexpectedly recovers from a knife wound through his eye and brain

gist: A man made an unexpected and rapid recovery after a knife penetrated his eye and brain.
Doctors noted that the exact mechanism of his injury remains unclear, noting a history of depression.
Such low-velocity penetrating brain injuries carry high risks, yet fortunate recoveries have been documented historically.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A man suffered a knife wound through his eye and brain. Following intensive care and surgery to remove his breathing tube, he recovered rapidly. Scans showed healing with minor bleeding, swelling, and air in the brain tissue, but no infections or seizures occurred. His language function was preserved, and temporary right-side weakness resolved quickly. He was later discharged and remained well at follow-up appointments.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Injuries going through the eye and brain are rare and typically involve high-velocity mechanisms like gunshots. Knives are rarer low-velocity mechanisms that carry substantial morbidity and mortality. This case highlights that outcomes may depend on precise trajectory relative to critical structures rather than external severity.

fivew: An unnamed man with a history of depression

timeline.text: This man refused life-saving treatment because of his religion - days later the rules changed

gist: Isaac Valdez died refusing a blood transfusion due to his Jehovah's Witness beliefs.
Days later, the Jehovah's Witnesses Governing Body changed its policy on blood components.
The policy shift has sparked grief, anger, and questions among former and current followers.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Isaac Valdez suffered a brain haemorrhage following a seizure. As a Jehovah's Witness, he refused a life-saving blood transfusion and died when his life support was turned off. Just 23 days later, the Jehovah's Witnesses' Governing Body announced that followers may now accept medical treatments using blood components.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The long-standing ban on blood transfusions, in place for 81 years, led to deaths and family heartbreak. The sudden policy change has left grieving relatives questioning why the leadership did not act sooner, while some followers feel their faith has been shaken.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The leadership has stated that individuals who previously left the faith because of the blood policy are warmly welcomed back if they wish to return.

He followed the Jehovah's Witnesses' prohibition on blood transfusions.

sections.text: A severe moorland and forest fire engulfed 25 square kilometres in the Cairngorms. Months later, the writer visited the charred area, noting widespread blackness, charcoal pines, and ongoing dangers like falling trees and hotspots. Despite the damage, some areas show surprising resilience with blooming bog asphodel and active black grouse.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The fire drastically altered the landscape, destroying thick heather and damaging roots and peat in the forest. However, restoration efforts are underway as a group planted over 3,000 native montane trees grown from nearby seeds. Additionally, natural regeneration is visible through emerging deer-grass, birch shoots, bracken, and fire-loving fungi.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Landscape restoration programmes will continue in the area, supported by ongoing tree-planting initiatives and the natural emergence of new growth and pyrophilous fungi in the charcoal.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Luke Alfano set up Too Young to Grieve, a support community offering young people aged 18 to 35 a space to talk about loss. Founded after Alfano lost his father and grandmother, the group has expanded to more than 20 locations, including London, Manchester, the US, Australia, and Belfast. Members meet for activities such as walks, pottery painting, and football tournaments.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Young adults often feel isolated when facing bereavement because few peers share their experience. Members like Chris Guiller, Katherine Macauley, and William Gregg say the community helps them realise they are not alone and gives them a safe space to process grief and protect their mental health.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Statutory guidance published by the Department for Education requires primary and secondary school lessons on loss and bereavement from September 2026. However, Northern Ireland does not have equivalent statutory guidance, relying instead on pastoral care policies and curriculum resources.

gist: Flesh won the final series of Drag Race UK broadcast by the BBC.
The BBC cancelled the programme as a result of financial pressures and budget cuts.
The show will move to a streaming platform run by its production company.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: RuPaul crowned London performer Flesh as the series eight winner following the final episode. Twelve contestants competed throughout ten weeks before the broadcaster announced the cancellation of the series due to budget cuts. Flesh received a cash prize of £25,000.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The programme will transition to a subscription streaming service owned by the production company, which causes worries about reduced audiences and fewer opportunities for performers. Some fans hope the move might bring larger cash prizes.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The UK edition of the series will move to Wow Presents Plus, marking a new chapter for the programme after its departure from the BBC.

fivew: RuPaul crowned a new winner as the BBC cancelled the UK series.
The BBC decided to axe the programme because of financial pressures and budget cuts.

quotes.text: This is where it feels slightly sadder that we're leaving the BBC because for all of the parameters that it created that limited what we could do, there was more exposure than drag has ever been given

gist: Cristiano Ronaldo has announced his retirement from international football for Portugal.
The 41-year-old forward holds world records for both goals scored and caps earned.
Ronaldo leaves the national team after a career spanning twenty-three years.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football at the age of 41. The forward, who debuted for Portugal in 2003, announced his decision via an Instagram video. His departure follows an incident last month where he left the national camp after being informed he would not start in a Nations League match against Denmark.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Ronaldo concludes his international career as a record-breaker, having earned 234 caps and scored 146 goals for his country. He described the decision as difficult, noting that it was made with both his mind and heart.

fivew: Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football.
The announcement was made after a career spanning from 2003 to the present.
The announcement was made via an Instagram video.
He stated that the time has come to pass the shirt on to the future.

quotes.text: the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt
A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to and end.

gist: The Formula 1 season continues in Sao Paulo with championship battles ongoing.
Ferrari drivers held talks following a first-lap collision in Mexico.
Red Bull and McLaren aim for improvements as the season nears its end.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The Sao Paulo Grand Prix marks the start of the final phase of the championship. Mercedes aims to secure the constructors' title. Meanwhile, Ferrari held clear-the-air talks following tension between team-mates Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc after they tangled on the first lap in Mexico.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Positions in the standings affect prize money and provide motivation for next season. Red Bull and McLaren are closely contested for third place with significant financial amounts on the line. Teams are also using the remaining races to gather data and prepare for the 2027 championship battle.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Teams will compete in Sao Paulo followed by three potential remaining races in Las Vegas, Qatar, and Abu Dhabi, though doubt remains regarding the Gulf events due to the conflict in the Middle East.

gist: Frank Lampard questioned decisions in Coventry defeat at Everton.
Coventry were denied a penalty after a hair pull.
Managers disagreed over controversial match incidents.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Everton beat Coventry 3-1 after goals from Thierno Barry and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall following Yann Gboho's opener. Coventry manager Frank Lampard questioned three major decisions going against his side, including a penalty appeal for hair pulling.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Lampard felt decisions regarding a hair pull, a challenge on Taiwo Awoniyi and a potential handball by Barry changed the game. Everton boss David Moyes disagreed over the handball and criticised the hair pull rule.

fivew: Coventry lost 3-1 to Everton after controversial refereeing and VAR decisions.
Disagreements arose over penalties and handball decisions during the match.

quotes.text: They're saying it's not enough of a pull and I think it's a hard area to be in.
